title: Critical Status of the Endangered Limpet Patella candei in the Canary Islands: Historical Population Trend and Environmental Stressors
content:
ABSTRACT

The Macaronesian endemic limpet Patella candei, also known as the ‘majorera limpet’, is an endangered species with a restricted distribution limited to Fuerteventura (Canary Islands) and the Selvagens Islands (Madeira). This study assessed its current distribution and conservation status in Fuerteventura through field surveys conducted in 2022, complemented by a historical comparison with previously published data. The results revealed that the species has become extinct in Lobos Islet and along the northern and eastern coasts of Fuerteventura, with only a relict population persisting in the southern region of the Jandia peninsula. Although the number of individuals in this area has increased in recent years, the population remains very low and insufficient for successful reproduction. This population also shows a broad size distribution, possibly linked to the area's strong wave exposure, which may reduce harvesting pressure by limiting accessibility. Despite the implementation of a recovery plan in 2015, the species continues to decline, suggesting that current conservation efforts have been insufficient. To explore whether oceanographic variables may have influenced this decline, anomalies in air temperature and sea surface temperature were analysed, revealing a warming trend over recent decades. These findings highlight the poor conservation status of P. candei in Fuerteventura and underscore the urgent need for enhanced management and conservation measures to prevent further population decline and potential extinction.
